t:
(a) The Study Commission shall be composed of the Secretary of the Interior, the Administrator of General Services, the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution, the Chairman of the Council on the Arts and Humanities, the Chairman of the National Capital Planning Commission, the Chairman of the Commission of Fine Arts, six Members of the Senate, three from each party, to be appointed by the President of the Senate, and six Members of the House of Representatives, three from each party, to be appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives, and three additional members appointed by the President, at least two of whom shall not be officers of the Federal Government. Non-Federal members shall serve at the pleasure of the President. The Secretary of the Interior shall be the Chairman of the Study Commission. The Study Commission shall meet at the call of the Chairman. 
    (b) Members of the Study Commission who are not officers or employees of the Federal or District Government shall be entitled to receive compensation in accordance with section 15 of the ‘Act of August 2, 1946 (5 U.S.C. 55a), and travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, as authorized by law (5 U.S.C. 73b–z) for persons in the Government service employed intermittently. 
    (c) The Director of the National Park Service, in consultation with the Administrator of the General Services Administration shall provide necessary staff and facilities to assist the Commission in carrying out its duties under this Act.

fable.w: The tempting reading is "No", because most of the Study Commission's members are federal officials and Members of Congress, and the consultation in subsection (c) is purely between federal agencies. But the section requires that at least two presidential appointees not be federal officers, and subsection (b) provides compensation and per diem for those non-federal members. That brings people outside the federal government onto a commission, which meets the definition of participation.
fable.s: three additional members appointed by the President, at least two of whom shall not be officers of the Federal Government

qwen_block.w: The section establishes a Study Commission that explicitly includes members who are not officers of the Federal Government. The definition states that participation includes advisory committees or commissions that include non-federal members. The presence of these outside members on the commission constitutes participation in the federal decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: three additional members appointed by the President, at least two of whom shall not be officers of the Federal Government.

opus.w: The Study Commission must include at least two non-federal members, and subsection (b) gives per diem pay to members who are not federal or District employees. That brings people from outside the federal government into the commission's work. The tempting 'No' reading treats this as an all-federal body because most members are agency heads or Members of Congress. But the required non-federal seats cross the federal boundary, as with the commissions in Examples 4 and 8.
opus.s: three additional members appointed by the President, at least two of whom shall not be officers of the Federal Government. Non-Federal members shall serve at the pleasure of the President.
opus.b: Most members of the Study Commission are federal officials or Members of Congress, which would make this "No" if they were the only members. That reading fails because the President must appoint at least two members who are not federal officers. Subsection (b) also pays per diem to members outside the federal and District governments, which confirms that outsiders are included. In the worked examples, a commission with non-federal members counts as participation, even when its exact role in decisions is unclear.

qwen_chat.w: The section establishes a Study Commission that includes members who are not officers of the Federal Government. The definition of participation includes advisory committees or commissions that include non-federal members. Since the commission includes outsiders (non-federal members) who participate in the commission's duties, this constitutes participation.
qwen_chat.s: three additional members appointed by the President, at least two of whom shall not be officers of the Federal Government. Non-Federal members shall serve at the pleasure of the President.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue "No" because the majority of the commission members are federal officials (Secretary of Interior, Administrator of GSA, Senators, Representatives), and the definition states that Congress and federal agencies are inside the government. However, the definition explicitly states that participation includes an advisory committee that includes *non-federal members*. The presence of even some non-federal members brings the process outside the federal boundary.
